full_judgment:
Mr. Sikder Maqbul Huq, J: This revisional application at the instance of the plaintiff petitioner is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27.10.98 passed by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 201 of 1997 reversing those of the Subordinate Judge, Artha kin Adalat, Comilla dismissing the Title Suit No. 9 of 1996. 

 4. Further case of the plaintiff is that while he was serving as manager of Daulatpur Bazar branch in the district of Manikganj he allowed over draft of Tk. 24,900/- to M/S. Nabaron Pharmacy on proper security and thereafter, on being transferred to Babu Bazar branch, Dhaka, he handed over charge to Mr. Shafiqul Bari Khan, who did not take any steps to realise the aforesaid advance. Thus the head office of the bank made Mr. Shafiqul Bad Khan liable for non-realization of the debt by its letters dated 9.2.87 and 6.4.87. The plaintiff petitioner also made some advance to one Matiur Rahman on proper security while he was working as manager of Daulatpur branch and his successor manager Mr. Shafiqul Bad Khan filed a money suit for realization of the outstanding balance and the suit ended in a com-promise decree. Thereafter the petitioner was served with a show cause notice on various charges wherein as many as 12 charges were brought against him and he was asked to show cause as to why he would not be dismissed from service. The petitioner replied to show cause which was considered to be not satisfactory and inquiry officer was appointed. The appointed Inquiry Officer found him guilty of minor charges such as making of unauthorized advances. The Board of Directors having considered the inquiry report, rein-stead the plaintiff petitioner in service on 4.4.84 with a condition that he would be responsible for realization of outstanding balance of M/S. Nabaron Pharmacy. The plaintiff was ultimately dismissed from service on the ground that he could not realize the loan money improperly advanced by him to MIS, Nabaron Pharmacy. Plaintiffs petitioner's further contention is that he approached the authority to allow him to serve in Daulatpur Branch for the purpose of realizing of the outstanding balance but the authority did not pay heed to it and further the plaintiff was made to attend his office on each working day during the long period of suspension from 16.5.81. Plaintiff received the dismissal order on 21.l.91 and thereafter filed to the Board of Directors an application for review on 20.2.91 which was not considered and rejected on 3.6.91. Thus the plaintiff was constrained to bring the suit as aforesaid. 

 6. Mrs. Farida Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner submits that the court of appeal below committed a substantial error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in reversing the judgment arid decree passed by the learned Trial Court. The learned Advocate emphatically contended that the impugned order of dismissal of the petitioner is illegal, malafide and motivated as the defendant bank having failed to establish the charge brought against him for man-handling etc. dismissed him from service for an offence for which he was earlier punished. She further submits that the impugned order is also illegal and void on the ground that the plaintiff petitioner was not charged in accordance with the service rules of the defendant bank and 2nd show cause notice as required by law was not served upon him before his dismissal from the service. The learned Advocate has also contended that in fact no proceeding as required by the service rule... of the defendant bank was drawn against the plaintiff petitioner and as such the impugned order is illegal, without jurisdiction and null and void. 

 8. There is no dispute about the fact that the plaintiff petitioner was an officer of the defendant bank and while he was serving as manager of Daulatpur Branch of the defendant bank. he received as show cause notice on charge of misappropriation of bank money by criminal breach of trust, misconduct, making unauthorized advances etc. and an inquiry officer was ultimately appointed to inquire into the matter and the inquiry officer found the petitioner guilty of making unauthorized advance to M/S. Nabaron Pharmacy and also to one Matiur Rahman and the bank authority considering the inquiry report and other aspects of the case re-instead the petitioner to his service on 4-4-1984 with the condition as aforesaid. There is also no dispute about the fact that the petitioner was transferred from the Daulatpur Branch, Manikganj, to Babu Bazar Branch, Dhaka and there was no scope for him to pursue realization of the alleged unauthorized advance either from the M/S Nabaron Pharmacy or from Mr. Matiur Rahman. There is also no dispute about the fact that the successor manager Shafiqul Bari Khan instituted a money suit against said Matiur Rahman for realization of the outstanding balance and the suit ended in a compromise decree and thereby the demand of the bank was satisfied. Petitioner's contention is that Mr. Shafiqul Bari did not take any step for realisation of the outstanding balance from MIS. Nabaron Pharmacy and (he defendant bank held Mr. Shafiqul Bari responsible for such negligence vide orders dated 9.2.87 and 6.4.87. 

 The plaintiff was not convicted in the criminal case and as such second condition has got no bearing so far as the mat-ter before us is concerned. The first condition was that the plaintiff would remain liable for realisation of the concerned unauthorised advances made by him within reasonable period failing which further disciplinary action would be initiated against him. This further disciplinary action to be initiated against plaintiff petitioner does not in any way refer to a second show cause notice rather it clearly indicates that a fresh proceeding for failure on his part to realise the concerned unauthorised advance made by him within a reasonable period will be started. The defendant bank started a fresh proceeding against plaintiff petitioner and served a notice dated 28.7.90 asking him to show cause as to why he would not be dismissed from the service of the bank for the charges established against him in the earlier inquiry vide the inquiry report sub-mitted on 10.8.90 by inquiry officer. It may, in this connection, be mentioned that the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner has brought to our notice that in the earlier proceeding was brought against the petitioner for his failure to realise the concerned unauthorised advanced made by him. In this connection it can further be said that the alleged unauthorised advances to Mr. Matiur Rahman was satisfied in pursuance of Court's decree and the petitioner while working as Manager of the Daulatpur branch it appears from the record, realised Tk. 8,200/- from M/S Nabaron Pharmacy and this fact has not been controverted by the opposite parties. It further appears from the record that no charge was levelled against the plaintiff-petitioner that he could not realise any of the unauthorized advances made by him during his tenure of service as Manager, Daulatpur I3ranch. and as such his subsequent dis-missal from his service on the ground that he failed to realise the money definitely offends against the principle of natural justice and the dismissal order as con-tended by the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner must be termed as illegal malafide and without jurisdiction particularly in view of the failure of the sub-sequent proceeding drawn against him. It may further be mentioned that the notice dated 28.7.90 is not a 2nd show cause notice but starting of a fresh proceeding as contemplated by condition No. 1 of the order of the reinstatement. Further it may be reiterated that a departmental proceeding having terminated either in minor or major punishment or even in discharge cannot be revived and there is no such provision in the rules framed by the bank for taking disciplinary action against delinquents. Delinquent officer or employee cannot be punished twice for the same offence and the defendant bank completely misdirected itself in dismissing the plaintiff from his service and the dis-missal order in this view of this aspect as the ease, also must be held to be without jurisdiction and void. 

 14. In view of the above facts and circumstances and material evidence on record we are of the view that the suit of file plaintiff was maintainable and the learned appellate court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 15. In the result, the rule is made absolute and the judgment and decree passed by the learned 'Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 201 of 1997 reversing those of the trial court are hereby set aside. Judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat are restored.
